newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Nov 29.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Nov 29.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

The National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) said on Friday it planned to buy back on market up to 74 million shares at a cost of about A$1.1 billion at current market prices. It also said it was working with an international investment bank to finalise a new flexible capital instrument that would raise up to US$750 million and raise NAB's level of tier one capital. NAB managing director Don Argus said this provided strategic flexibility, "particularly in taking advantage of acquisition opportunities."
Mayne Nickless Ltd said on Friday the float of its Optus Communications shareholding would not now take place this calendar year because of Optus Vision shareholder litigation.

Dutch postal and telecommunications group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) said on Friday that its takeover bid for TNT would be declared unconditional if its stake rises above 50 percent and includes at least 105 million shares owned by Bankers Trust. KPN had previously said the A$2.45 per share bid would be unconditional from 90 percent.
Shares in UK mining group RTZ Corp rebounded on Thursday as copper prices climbed to a six-month high at the London Metals Exchange, dealers said. RTZ shares closed up 18.5 p at 9.84 stg.
The Adelaide Steamship Co Ltd has appointed brokers to advise on either a A$150 million equity raising or a float of its Adsteam Marine business, The Sydney Morning Herald reported on Friday.
Diversified manufacturer Futuris Corp Ltd said it was marketing a A$150 million bond issue, managed by SBC Warburg, which was expected to be finalised on December 20.
Pay television operator Australis Media Ltd said on Thursday it appointed former MovieVision and Seven Network executive Sean O'Halloran as chief executive.
